subject: gk
question: Which of the following describes the Medhi part in Buddhist structure?

options.text: Ceremonial gateways in front of stupas
The circular terrace between the railing and dome
A low wall to enclose the structure
The umbrella-shaped structure placed at the top of the structure

solution:
The correct answer is __**The circular terrace between the railing and dome**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Medhi is the circular terrace found in the structure of a Buddhist stupa.
 
• It is located between the railing (Vedika) and the dome (Anda) of the stupa.
 
• The Medhi is an important part of the architectural design of stupas, providing a platform for circumambulation (Pradakshina) by devotees.
 
• This terrace is often decorated and serves as a transitional element between the lower and upper parts of the stupa.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vedika:** The railing around the stupa, which encloses the sacred area and provides a boundary for the Medhi.
 
• **Anda:** The dome-shaped structure representing the mound of earth, symbolizing the universe and the burial mound of the relics of the Buddha.
 
• **Chhatra:** The umbrella-like structure placed at the top of the stupa, symbolizing honor and respect.
 
• **Torana:** Ceremonial gateways that are often positioned at the cardinal points around the stupa, marking entrances to the sacred path.
 
• **Pradakshina Patha:** The circumambulatory path around the stupa, used by devotees for ritualistic walking in a clockwise direction to show reverence.
